score.note: Two independent divergence clusters remain, both scheduling/register-allocation shaped rather than missing statements. Reusing the already-proved serial_error carrier for REG_IME=1 removes the spurious literal and improves the canonical result from 234/38/40 to 232/34/29. The reference still loads the REG_IE address later and derives the byte mask from the live one carrier. In the tail, the reference reloads SERIAL_RUNTIME after the two calls and keeps that new pointer in r7; caching the earlier pointer is semantically invalid because the calls may replace the global. The residual remains Draft C and claims zero DONE bytes.

exact_closure_revalidation: 2026-08-31: complete serial-runtime TU scoring reproduces 232/234 bytes, differing_halfwords=34, wrong_instructions=29, and equal branch topology. The decoder reports no unique source shape and all eight literal-pool words are exact. The named live-carrier repair is either byte-neutral under u8 folding or sharply regressive under s8; canonical source was restored. Together with the recorded condition, statement, width, tail-pointer, and canonical-pass matrix, this is an honestly bounded blocker; no adoption or DONE bytes are claimed.

rejected_experiments.experiment: decoder/aligned-diff named carrier repair: after REG_IME=1, spell the reference's live-one mask as `serial_error -= 66; byte &= serial_error` instead of `byte &= ~0x40`
rejected_experiments.result: byte-identical to the 232/34/29 baseline: GCC constant-folds the u8 carrier back to movs #191. Changing only serial_error to signed s8 prevents that fold but regresses to 236 bytes, differing_halfwords 87, wrong_instructions 55. Both forms were rejected and canonical source restored.
